name: UART TCP
description: This component allows bytes to be transferred between a hardware [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart/) and a TCP socket. Data is copied unchanged in both directions.

config_entries.label: UART ID
config_entries.description: The [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart/) to use. This component needs the UART for itself: another component with the same `uart_id`, or `dummy_receiver` in the UART's [debug](https://esphome.io/components/uart/#debugging) option, is rejected. A `uart.write` action or a lambda that uses the UART is not detected, so avoid them.

config_entries.label: Host
config_entries.description: The host to connect to. An IPv4 address or a hostname. IPv6 is not supported. This option cannot be used when `role` is `server`.

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: The TCP port to connect to, or to listen on. When `role` is `server`, a second `uart_tcp` or `tcp_uart` server on the same port is rejected.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Allowed Ips
config_entries.description: IPv4 addresses that may connect. A plain address is one host. A network is written in CIDR form, for example `192.0.2.0/24`. At most 255 entries. If the option is omitted, every address may connect. A rejected client is closed immediately and logged as a warning at most once every 5 seconds; an IPv6 client is rejected unless it carries an IPv4 mapped address, as on a dual stack network. This option cannot be used when `role` is `client`.

config_entries.label: Reconnect Interval
config_entries.description: The time to wait before trying again after a failure. An unanswered connection attempt is given up after `reconnect_interval` or 10 seconds, whichever is longer. Defaults to `5s`.
